newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares in sharp recovery, drugs lead.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares in sharp recovery, drugs lead.

text.p: Swedish shares joined optimistic European bourses in a sharp rise on Tuesday as blue chips rebounded from falls on Monday. Drugs major Astra led a 2.1 percent increase in the index-heavy sector.
The all-share index rose 1.18 percent to 2,039.97 in moderate turnover of 2.4 billion crowns.

Ericsson gained three crowns to 166.5 to match Monday's closing price in New York. The share peaked at 167 crowns but was hit by a negative sentiment to the sector following the U.S. AT&T's profit warning for the third quarter.
Astra, too, gained from positive sentiment on Wall Street in Monday's trade, and the share closed six crowns higher to 277 crowns, piloting a 2.1 percent hike in the sector index.

The banking and insurance sector calmed down after rumours of a merger between giants S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken sent shares in the two companies soaring on Monday. S-E-Banken gained 0.50 crowns to 60, but Handelsbanken fell 0.50 to 155 crowns.
Other bank shares fared better. Foreningsbanken jumped 1.60 crowns or 6.2 percent to a new all-time high of 27.30, and Nordbanken also hit an all-time high of 162.50, up four crowns on the day.
"Reports on talks between the banks have affected the entire industry. It might well start of speculation about other banks," one broker said.
Volvo climbed three crowns to 145 crowns.
